summary: This note is a section of the history of Chelsea F.C. covering the 1963-72 seasons, when the club regularly challenged for honours and won several trophies. It then describes a decline caused largely by debt from an ambitious redevelopment of Stamford Bridge, and a revival under John Neal in the mid-1980s that brought a Second Division title and a return to the top flight.
one_line: Covers Chelsea F.C.'s 1960s-70s trophy successes, the debt-driven near-collapse after the Stamford Bridge redevelopment, and John Neal's mid-1980s revival.
key_facts: The 1963-72 seasons saw Chelsea F.C. regularly challenge for honours for the first time, although they often narrowly missed out.
Chelsea F.C. won the League Cup in 1965.
Chelsea F.C. won the FA Cup in 1970.
Chelsea F.C. won the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup in 1971.
Chelsea F.C. were FA Cup runners-up in 1967.
Chelsea F.C. were League Cup runners-up in 1972.
Several problems over the following decade, principally the debt burden caused by an ambitious attempt to redevelop Stamford Bridge, brought Chelsea F.C. to the brink of extinction.
A revival under John Neal in the mid-1980s saw Chelsea F.C. win the Second Division title.
The revival under John Neal ultimately re-established Chelsea F.C. in the top flight.
